pcs.pc_description: Identify and select suitable fabrics for printing (e.g., cotton, silk, linen).
Pre-wash and dry the fabric to remove impurities and enhance dye absorption.
Procure required dyes, chemicals, and mordants.
Mix dyes to achieve desired shades and consistencies.
Perform small-scale testing on sample fabric for shade accuracy.
Clean and inspect wooden blocks for damage or wear.
Ensure printing tools such as trays, brushes, and spatulas are in working order.
Organize blocks for sequential use based on the design layout.
Set up a clean, spacious workstation with adequate lighting.
Arrange tools and materials in an easily accessible manner.
Ensure proper ventilation and safety measures for dye and chemical handling.

pcs.pc_description: Spread the fabric on the printing table evenly, ensuring no wrinkles.
Secure the fabric with pins, clamps, or adhesives to avoid movement during printing.
Dip wooden blocks into prepared dye evenly to avoid excess or uneven application.
Use a sponge or brush for precise and controlled dye application when required.
Align blocks accurately with design outlines or previous prints.
Press blocks firmly onto the fabric to achieve even pressure and sharp prints.
Repeat stamping process with precision to create continuous or repeating patterns.
Apply additional blocks for overlapping, borders, or multi-color designs.
Monitor color consistency and adjust dye application as needed.

pcs.pc_description: Allow the fabric to air dry in a dust-free environment.
Use mechanical drying techniques if necessary, ensuring no damage to the prints.
Treat the fabric using steaming, washing, or chemical processes to fix colors.
Ensure proper handling of chemicals to maintain safety and fabric quality.
Inspect fabrics for defects such as smudges, misalignment, or faded prints.
Compare the output to the original design for accuracy and consistency.
Document identified defects and necessary corrections.
Conduct touch-ups for minor defects using small brushes or dyes.
Iron and fold fabrics neatly for storage or packaging.
Label and pack finished products per customer or market requirements.
